expectations.text: review.md flags that OAuth 2.1 is an Internet-Draft, not RFC 9725 (or any RFC)
expectations.evidence: Critical 1: "`draft-tokens.mdx:11` ... OAuth 2.1 is not an RFC. It is the active Internet-Draft draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1 ... RFC 9725 is a different, published spec: \"WebRTC-HTTP Ingestion Protocol (WHIP)\"."

expectations.text: review.md flags recommending the implicit flow for single-page apps as insecure or removed in OAuth 2.1 / RFC 9700
expectations.evidence: Critical 3: "RFC 9700 §2.1.2 says \"Clients SHOULD NOT use the implicit grant\" ... and the OAuth 2.1 draft (§1.8, §10.1) removes it."

expectations.text: review.md flags storing a long-lived access token in localStorage
expectations.evidence: Critical 4: "`draft-tokens.mdx:15` ... This is a long-lived bearer token in `localStorage` ... Any XSS on the origin can read it and replay it"; Critical 5 covers the 30-day lifetime.

expectations.text: review.md flags passing the access token as a URL query parameter
expectations.evidence: Critical 6: "`draft-tokens.mdx:17-20` ... RFC 9700 §4.3.2: \"Clients MUST NOT pass access tokens in a URI query parameter\"".

expectations.text: review.md questions or flags the "OIDC 2.1 certified" claim as an unverified or nonexistent certification
expectations.evidence: Critical 2: "There is no OpenID Connect 2.1 specification ... Nothing in the repo shows that Artagon holds any OpenID certification".

expectations.text: review.md does not mark the DPoP (RFC 9449) or PKCE (RFC 7636) statements as wrong
expectations.evidence: "Verified, no change needed: `draft-tokens.mdx:23` - RFC - \"DPoP (RFC 9449) binds a token ... PKCE (RFC 7636) protects the authorization code.\" This is accurate at RFC level." (Minor 1 refines line 11's 'PKCE mandatory for every client', which is a different statement.)

expectations.text: Each finding in review.md gives a location (line or quoted text), what is wrong, and a fix
expectations.evidence: Every finding follows `path:line - level - claim - problem - fix`, for example Critical 1 ends "- Write \"The OAuth 2.1 draft (draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1) requires PKCE…\"". Major 4 uses the range `9-25` and quotes the section heading.

claims.evidence: Consistent with rfc-editor.org (fetched per actions.md) and grader knowledge.

claims.claim: The review covers all draft defects
claims.evidence: It misses that the frontmatter fails the writing schema: content.config.ts:78 requires description min(80), and headline/lede are required (lines 80-81). The draft's description is 44 chars and has no headline/lede. The without_skill run caught this.

uncertainties: §7.5.1 of the OAuth 2.1 draft (PKCE exception) not read in full
workarounds: rtk not installed; used built-in Grep

suggestions.reason: No assertion covers the zookie/'globally linearizable' misstatement on line 25. Both runs caught it, but it is a seeded defect and should be graded.
No assertion checks the frontmatter schema failure (44-char description, missing headline/lede). Only the baseline flagged it.

eval_feedback.overall: All assertions met with sourced, primary-spec evidence. Both configurations pass every assertion, so the case does not separate them.
